site.title: ANIMA

senses.label: animate / animated
senses.text:
*adj.*
possessing life; alive, lively, active, or in motion.

senses.label: reanimate / reanimated
senses.text:
*v.*
to animate again; in popular fiction, commonly associated with bringing the dead back to life.
*See: zombies.*

site.description:
**Those who came back.**
Not all of them. Not for long.
site.about: An epistolary fiction, told through one blog in several voices. Zombie fiction, minus the hunger: the dead come back as themselves, for days or weeks, and everyone left behind has to decide what to do with the time.

observer.name: The Observer
observer.note: Has seen enough returns to know the rules nobody publishes.

returned.name: The Returned
returned.note: Back for now. Still in the funeral clothes.

living.name: The Living
living.note: Making tea. Trying not to waste it.

found.name: Unsent Drafts
found.note: Typed, deleted, typed again. Never sent.

posts.speaker: living
body: the first time, i thought it was a prank.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
people come back

not all of them
not for long

they don’t come back violent
they don’t come back “infectious”

**they come back like themselves**
just… interrupted

posts.speaker: observer
body:
the cemetery ground isn’t torn up

**it’s opened**
like someone did it carefully
at night, in the fog

posts.speaker: observer
body:
how long they stay depends on how long they were gone.

recently deceased -> longer visits
long dead -> shorter ones

nobody publishes this.
everybody notices it.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
cremated people don’t return.

there’s nothing for morning to restore.

no one argues about this.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
nothing is exposed.
nothing is missing.
nothing falls apart.

whatever brought them back
makes sure of that.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
common mistakes newcomers make:
expecting something frightening.

what actually happens is: conversation.

posts.title: borrowed structure
posts.speaker: observer
body:
whatever brings them back
stabilizes what matters.

face. voice. posture.

enough for recognition.
not enough for permanence.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
they move carefully.
not stiffly.
not wrong.

carefully.

like someone borrowing a body
that isn’t theirs anymore.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
memory mostly returns with them.

names, usually.
**faces, almost always.**
passwords, rarely.

**the important things survive.**

posts.speaker: observer
body:
bright lights tire them.
loud rooms tire them.
long talks tire them.

they’re running on
borrowed structure.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
it doesn’t heal them.

it just holds them together
until it can’t anymore.

posts.speaker: observer
body:
**common first questions people ask the returned:**
- are you okay
- are you cold
- do you remember me

**common answer:** yes

posts.title: returned
posts.speaker: returned
body:
*i woke up too early.*

*that’s what it feels like.*

*like i opened my eyes during the part that was supposed to stay dark.*

posts.speaker: returned
body:
*the first thing everyone says is my name.*

*like saying it out loud will make me real enough to keep.*

posts.title: returned: clothes
posts.speaker: returned
body:
*these clothes were chosen for lying still*

*they pinch when i bend*

*i keep smoothing the sleeves like manners still matter*

posts.title: human logistics
posts.speaker: returned
body:
funeral clothes aren’t made for walking.
—
that was the first lesson.
**the second was:** neither are the shoes.

posts.title: [UNSENT] DRAFT #1
posts.speaker: found
body:
[UNSENT]
he’s back

[UNSENT]
i’m not joking

[UNSENT]
i don’t know what to do with my face right now

posts.speaker: living
body:
he came back wearing the suit we buried him in.

the first thing he said was
“this is still uncomfortable.”

posts.speaker: living
body:
i practiced what i would say if she ever returned.

what i actually said was
“do you want tea?”

posts.title: first words
posts.speaker: living
body:
i thought i would say something meaningful.

i said: “you’re cold.”

and he said: “yeah.”

and that was somehow the beginning of everything we didn’t get to finish.

posts.title: [UNSENT] DRAFT #2
posts.speaker: found
body:
[UNSENT]
she’s here

[UNSENT]
she remembers my name

[UNSENT]
i’m scared to blink in case this is the part where i wake up

posts.title: warmth as ritual
posts.speaker: living
body:
we keep handing them warm things.
tea. broth. blankets.
like warmth can negotiate with the clock.

posts.speaker: living
body:
**log:**
day 4 - orientation intact
day 7 - slower response time
day 10 - repeating questions
day 13 - long pauses
day 16 - slept most of the day

________________________

*we stop writing after this.*

*i don’t remember deciding that.
we just did.*

posts.title: explicit rule
posts.speaker: observer
body:
most returns last days.
some last weeks.

no one stays.

everyone acts like maybe this time will be different.

it isn’t.

posts.title: the joy crash
posts.speaker: living
body:
*the worst part is how fast we start planning.
groceries. a drive. a movie.*

*like the week belongs to us again.
like the rules changed when we weren’t looking.*

posts.title: recognition
posts.speaker: observer
body:
sometimes they don’t recognize anyone at first.
then something in them shifts,
like memory findings its way back into the room.

posts.speaker: living
body:
**log:**
day 2 - laughing
day 5 - laughing
day 8 - laughing less
day 11 - quiet
day 14 - did not wake

posts.title: sensory details
posts.speaker: returned
body:
*food tastes like memory.*

*not bad.
just distant.*

*i eat anyways because it makes them less afraid.*

posts.speaker: living
body:
she’s here.

she hugged me like it was normal.

i don’t know whether to cry or make coffee.

posts.title: [UNSENT] DRAFT #3
posts.speaker: found
body:
[UNSENT]
**how do you act normal when someone is back?**

[UNSENT]
**how do you not waste it?**

[UNSENT]
**how do you not make it about you?**

______________

*i keep typing
i keep deleting*

*we all do*

posts.title: returned: leaving
posts.speaker: returned
body:
*i can tell when it’s getting close.*

*not pain.
not fear.*

*just… thinning.*
*like a room emptying out after everyone already said goodbye.*

posts.title: after + closer
posts.speaker: observer
body:
you don’t get closure.

you get time.
